# Adjudication Task — Chapter 273

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃273화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“안녕하십니까!”
  6|
  7|“안녕하십니까!”
  8|
  9|조폭 두목이 된 기분이다. 걸을 때마다 구십 도로 허리를 굽히며 사방에서 인사를 하는 신입 길드원들 때문에.
 10|
 11|상대는 이제 막 훈련소를 수료한 햇병아리들. 연차로 따지면 내가 한참 선배이긴 하다.
 12|
 13|‘이 바닥이 선후배를 좀 엄격히 따지긴 하지.’
 14|
 15|문제는 신입 길드원 중에는 나보다 나이가 많은 늦깎이 헌터들도 있다는 거다.
 16|
 17|“만나 뵙게 되어 영광입니다!”
 18|
 19|서른 중반은 넘어 보이는 신입이 눈을 초롱초롱하게 빛내며 허리를 숙였다.
 20|
 21|눈빛보다 더 번쩍거리는 정수리를 보자 마음이 아려 온다.
 22|
 23|“네. 힘내세요…….”
 24|
 25|“감사합니다!”
 26|
 27|“감사합니다!”
 28|
 29|메아리야, 뭐야.
 30|
 31|그리고 너희들한테 말한 거 아니다. 이 풍성충들아.
 32|
 33|내심 혀를 차며 신입들을 바라보다가, 문득 한 청년에 이르러서 시선이 멈췄다.
 34|
 35|‘쟤는 좀 하겠는데?’
 36|
 37|이번에 들어온 신입 중 가장 낫다. 느껴지는 기운도 그렇고, 동작 하나하나가 무인처럼 절제되어 있다.
 38|
 39|내 시선을 느낀 청년이 씩 웃으며 말했다.
 40|
 41|“안녕하십니까, 선배님.”
 42|
 43|확실히 다르다. 다른 신입들처럼 긴장하지도, 굽실거리지도 않는다.
 44|
 45|내 경험상 이런 녀석들은 딱 두 가지 부류로 나뉜다.
 46|
 47|그냥 쥐뿔도 없는데 자존심이 강하거나, 아니면 스스로의 실력에 자신이 있거나.
 48|
 49|지금 눈앞에 있는 녀석은 후자다.
 50|
 51|“거기 계신 분, 혹시 성함이?”
 52|
 53|“김진수라고 합니다. 훈련소 B급 과정을 수석으로 수료했습니다. 이번 레이드에서 맨 처음 골렘의 핵을 파괴한 사람도 저고요.”
 54|
 55|“그래요?”
 56|
 57|“네. A급 게이트는 처음이었는데, 생각보다 어렵지는 않았습니다.”
 58|
 59|재미있는 놈일세.
 60|
 61|자기 얼굴에 금칠하면서도 거리낌이 없다. 어딜 가도 제 밥그릇 하나는 잘 챙길 스타일이다.
 62|
 63|내가 물끄러미 바라보자 김진수가 넉살 좋게 웃었다.
 64|
 65|“그리고 말씀 편히 하셔도 됩니다. 선배님.”
 66|
 67|“초면이니까. 편해지면 말 놓을게요. 다른 분들도 마찬가지니 오늘처럼 크게 인사하는 건 생략했으면 좋겠네요.”
 68|
 69|“예!”
 70|
 71|“명심하겠습니다. 선배님!”
 72|
 73|“…….”
 74|
 75|귓등으로도 안 듣는구나.
 76|
 77|쩌렁쩌렁 울리는 시끄러운 소리에 복도 끝에 있는 사무실 문이 스르륵 열렸다.
 78|
 79|빳빳한 흰색 와이셔츠에 잘 다림질된 검은 슬랙스. 저런 복장으로 출근하는 헌터는 우리 길드에 딱 한 사람밖에 없다.
 80|
 81|“아침부터 활기차네요.”
 82|
 83|“너무 활기차서 문제죠.”
 84|
 85|CF 속 한 장면처럼 커피잔을 든 최 팀장이 사무실 안을 턱짓했다.
 86|
 87|“커피라도 한잔하면서 가라앉힙시다. 들어오세요.”
 88|
 89|
 90|
 91|* * *
 92|
 93|
 94|
 95|사무실 안은 넓고 쾌적했다. 최 팀장의 취향에 맞게 꾸며진 탓인지 곳곳에 명품 가구가 즐비했고, 책상 위에는 은색 명패가 놓여 있었다.
 96|
 97|
 98|
 99|[팀장 최민우]
100|
101|
102|
103|‘명패까지 비싸 보이네.’
104|
105|길드 하우스 이전과 신입 길드원 영입으로 돈이 엄청나게 들었을 텐데, 원명훈이 길드장으로 있던 스타 길드에서 천문학적인 금액의 합의금을 받아 냈다는 말이 사실인 모양이다.
106|
107|그런 생각을 하며 명패를 구경하는데, 블랙커피가 담긴 잔이 불쑥 내밀어졌다.
108|
109|최 팀장이 내 시선이 향해 있는 곳을 보더니 물었다.
110|
111|“하나 만들어 드려요? 명패.”
112|
113|“괜찮습니다. 딱히 직책도 없는데요, 뭘.”
114|
115|“직책이야 만들면 되죠. 총괄팀장. 본부장. 뭐든 말씀해 보세요.”
116|
117|“뭐든지?”
118|
119|“네.”
120|
121|“그럼 소소하게 길드장으로.”
122|
123|“…….”
124|
125|“농담입니다. 제가 길드장 하면 길드 망해요.”
126|
127|그리고 어차피 해 봤자 얼굴마담, 바지사장일 게 뻔한데 뭘.
128|
129|나는 커피잔을 받아 들고 소파에 앉았다. 유리 테이블 위에는 20여 부가 넘는 신문들이 쌓여 있었다.
130|
131|국내 주요 일간지부터 당최 알아볼 수 없는 글자로 가득한 해외 신문까지. 보기만 해도 눈알이 팽팽 돌아가는 기분이다.
132|
133|“설마 이걸 다 보시는 겁니까?”
134|
135|“해외 흐름도 파악하고 업계 정보도 수집할 겸 해서요. 별거 아닙니다. 5개 국어 정도만 해도 충분히 볼 수 있어요.”
136|
137|“…….”
138|
139|그 정도면 매우 별거인데. 5개 국어라니, 이 인간 도대체 어떤 인생을 살아온 걸까.
140|
141|나는 혀를 내두르며 펼쳐져 있는 신문 중 하나를 곁눈질했다.
142|
143|30대로 보이는 남자의 선명한 컬러 사진과 함께 굵게 칠해진 폰트가 눈에 들어온다.
144|
145|
146|
147|- 故정현우 헌터(사진 첨부)
148|
149|- 계속되는 사고. A급 헌터도 피해 갈 수 없는 죽음의 공간, 게이트.
150|
151|- 명동 길드, 뜻하지 않은 고인의 죽음에 유감…….
152|
153|
154|
155|그새 또 사고가 일어난 모양이다.
156|
157|‘명동 길드면 지훈이네 길드인데.’
158|
159|좀 더 자세히 보려던 그때, 우아하게 커피잔을 기울인 최 팀장이 말을 이었다.
160|
161|“평화 길드는 앞으로도 계속해서 커질 겁니다. 이미 B급 헌터 스무 명에 C급 이하 서른 명을 충원했으니까요. 이 정도면 이미 고일 대로 고여 버린 국내 시장에서도 유례없는 성장세죠.”
162|
163|그의 말마따나 평화 길드의 성장 속도는 무시무시했다.
164|
165|길드 창설 후 고작 4개월 남짓한 시간이 흘렀을 뿐인데, 이 기세만 유지한다면 중견 길드라고 불러도 부족하지 않다.
166|
167|‘물론 중견 길드에 비교하면 아직 소속 헌터 숫자가 많이 부족하긴 하지만.’
168|
169|그건 아직 뽑지 않아서지, 못 뽑아서가 아니다.
170|
171|당장 길드 홈페이지가 트래픽 초과로 다운된 것만 봐도 알 수 있다. 하루에도 수백 건의 입사 관련 문의가 빗발친다고 했다.
172|
173|“그리고 거기에는 제가 큰 역할을 했고요. 일등 공신.”
174|
175|“사실이죠.”
176|
177|최 팀장이 부드럽게 말을 이었다.
178|
179|“사실이긴 한데, 보너스는 안 드립니다.”
180|
181|“……눈치 빠르시네.”
182|
183|혹시 싶어서 살짝 찔러 봤는데 역시 씨알도 안 먹혔다.
184|
185|말없이 입맛을 다시는 나를 보며 최 팀장이 빙긋 웃었다.
186|
187|“하지만 부탁 하나만 들어주시면 긍정적으로 생각해 보겠습니다.”
188|
189|“부탁이 뭔데요?”
190|
191|“신입 길드원들을 잠시 맡아 주셨으면 합니다.”
192|
193|“……신입들이요?”
194|
195|“예. 고르고 골라서 뽑긴 했는데, 다들 재능은 있지만 아무래도 아직 어설픈 면이 많아서 말입니다.”
196|
197|“당연하죠. 초짜니까.”
198|
199|아무리 훈련소를 거친다고 해도 실전의 분위기는 공기부터가 다르다.
200|
201|막 수료식을 끝낸 상위 헌터보다 10년 짬밥 먹은 하위 헌터가 더 낫다는 말이 괜히 나오는 것이 아니다.
202|
203|“그런데 왜 그걸 저한테…… 다른 분들도 계시잖아요.”
204|
205|“안 그래도 오늘 아침에 김 집사님과 송이 씨에게 말해 뒀습니다. 돌아가면서 가르치자고요.”
206|
207|“뭐래요?”
208|
209|“수락하시던데요. 한 치의 망설임 없이, 아주 흔쾌히.”
210|
211|“……꺽정 아저씨는요?”
212|
213|“아직 말씀 못 드렸습니다. 출근 시간이 훨씬 지났는데 연락도 안 받으시네요.”
214|
215|힐끗 시간을 확인한 최 팀장이 재차 말을 이었다.
216|
217|“좋지 않겠습니까. 신입 길드원들도 진태경 씨가 지도해 주기를 바라고 있습니다. 많은 선택지 중에 우리 길드에 지원한 이유도 대부분 진태경 씨 때문이고요.”
218|
219|“그, 비행기 태워 주셔서 감사하긴 한데.”
220|
221|나는 뒤통수를 긁적였다.
222|
223|지금 무림에서는 암천이 마수를 드러냈고 적천강은 의식불명 상태다.
224|
225|현대에서 30일을 보낸다 해도 무림에서 흐르는 시간은 고작 세 시간. 시간적인 여유는 있지만, A급 게이트를 돌아도 모자랄 판에 햇병아리들 가르치는 건 딱히 메리트 있는 선택이 아니었다.
226|
227|그럴 거면 차라리 그 시간에 가족들과 함께하는 게 백 배는 낫지.
228|
229|“저는 빼 주세요. 길드 입장에서도 제가 그 친구들 가르치는 것보다 A급 게이트 하나 더 깨는 게 효율적이지 않을까요?”
230|
231|“효율적이라…….”
232|
233|“네, 효율.”
234|
235|“그럼 어쩔 수 없군요.”
236|
237|최 팀장의 입가에 불길한 웃음이 맺혔다.
238|
239|“우리 신입 길드원들, 잘 부탁드립니다.”
240|
241|“예?”
242|
243|“A급 게이트. 예약이 전부 다 꽉 찼습니다. 최소한 앞으로 1주일 동안은 어림도 없어요.”
244|
245|“거짓말하지 마! 이 사기꾼!”
246|
247|“정 못 믿으시겠으면 직접 보시든가요.”
248|
249|나는 최 팀장이 내민 종이를 확 낚아챘다. 종이에는 전국의 A급 게이트 예약 현황이 빼곡하게 적혀 있었다.
250|
251|빌어먹을, 진짜네.
252|
253|“이번 달 성과급 200% 드리죠. 레이드도 뛰고, 후배들도 가르치고. 훈훈하네요.”
254|
255|“…….”
256|
257|“아니면 집에서 노시든가요.”
258|
259|최 팀장의 입꼬리가 밉살맞게 올라간다.
260|
261|‘안 해!’라고 외치려던 그 순간, 시스템 알림이 울렸다.
262|
263|띠링.
264|
265|
266|
267|- 퀘스트, [안 해! 라고 하기에는 너무나 큰돈이었다.]가 생성되었습니다!
268|
269|
270|
271|퀘스트를 수락하시겠습니까?
272|
273|Y   /   N
274|
275|
276|
277|“어쩌시렵니까?”
278|
279|“…….”
280|
281|“승낙하신 것으로 알고 신입들 준비시키겠습니다. B급 게이트 몇 군데 잡아 놨거든요.”
282|
283|띠링.
284|
285|
286|
287|- 당신은 암묵적으로 동의했습니다.
288|
289|- 퀘스트를 수락하셨습니다!
290|
291|
292|
293|이런 시벌.
294|
295|
296|
297|* * *
298|
299|
300|
301|- 크르르르.
302|
303|몬스터의 거친 숨결이 사방에서 조여 온다. 스무 쌍의 불안한 시선이 주위를 훑었다.
304|
305|후욱, 후욱.
306|
307|호흡이 가빠지고 방패며 무기를 움켜쥔 손은 하얗게 질렸다.
308|
309|나는 까마득히 높이 솟은 나뭇가지에 걸터앉아 그 광경을 지켜봤다.
310|
311|표정은 없어도 머릿속은 심각한 고민으로 가득 차 있었다.
312|
313|‘저녁 뭐 먹지.’
314|
315|갈비를 먹을까, 아니면 오랜만에 오리 백숙을 먹을까.
316|
317|둘 다 포기하기에는 너무 아까운데…….
318|
319|“막아!”
320|
321|“딜러 뭐 해. 딜러!”
322|
323|찢어지는 비명에 문득 바라보니 난장판이다.
324|
325|십여 마리의 라이칸스로프들이 달려들어 방패 벽을 두드리고 있었다. 새파랗게 질린 탱커들이 주르륵 밀려 나간다.
326|
327|‘몬스터를 힘으로 상대하려고 하니까 밀리지.’
328|
329|물론 탱커만의 잘못은 아니다. 딜러들도 당황한 나머지 제 역할을 하지 못하고 있다.
330|
331|적절할 때 견제 공격이 들어오면 지금 같은 상황이 벌어지지도 않았겠지.
332|
333|레이드 시작 전 몇 번이나 주의하라고 했건만, 역시 똑같다.
334|
335|‘저거 곧 뚫리겠는데.’
336|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Output contract

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

{
"chapter": 1,
"decisions": [
{
"hunk_id": "H001",
"decision": "SOL",
"reason": "brief specific reason"
},

},
{

"reason": "brief specific reason"
}
]
}

Include exactly one decision for every numbered hunk, in hunk order. `replacement` is required only for `REPAIR`.

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 273

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃273화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“안녕하십니까!”
  6|
  7|“안녕하십니까!”
  8|
  9|조폭 두목이 된 기분이다. 걸을 때마다 구십 도로 허리를 굽히며 사방에서 인사를 하는 신입 길드원들 때문에.
 10|
 11|상대는 이제 막 훈련소를 수료한 햇병아리들. 연차로 따지면 내가 한참 선배이긴 하다.
 12|
 13|‘이 바닥이 선후배를 좀 엄격히 따지긴 하지.’
 14|
 15|문제는 신입 길드원 중에는 나보다 나이가 많은 늦깎이 헌터들도 있다는 거다.
 16|
 17|“만나 뵙게 되어 영광입니다!”
 18|
 19|서른 중반은 넘어 보이는 신입이 눈을 초롱초롱하게 빛내며 허리를 숙였다.
 20|
 21|눈빛보다 더 번쩍거리는 정수리를 보자 마음이 아려 온다.
 22|
 23|“네. 힘내세요…….”
 24|
 25|“감사합니다!”
 26|
 27|“감사합니다!”
 28|
 29|메아리야, 뭐야.
 30|
 31|그리고 너희들한테 말한 거 아니다. 이 풍성충들아.
 32|
 33|내심 혀를 차며 신입들을 바라보다가, 문득 한 청년에 이르러서 시선이 멈췄다.
 34|
 35|‘쟤는 좀 하겠는데?’
 36|
 37|이번에 들어온 신입 중 가장 낫다. 느껴지는 기운도 그렇고, 동작 하나하나가 무인처럼 절제되어 있다.
 38|
 39|내 시선을 느낀 청년이 씩 웃으며 말했다.
 40|
 41|“안녕하십니까, 선배님.”
 42|
 43|확실히 다르다. 다른 신입들처럼 긴장하지도, 굽실거리지도 않는다.
 44|
 45|내 경험상 이런 녀석들은 딱 두 가지 부류로 나뉜다.
 46|
 47|그냥 쥐뿔도 없는데 자존심이 강하거나, 아니면 스스로의 실력에 자신이 있거나.
 48|
 49|지금 눈앞에 있는 녀석은 후자다.
 50|
 51|“거기 계신 분, 혹시 성함이?”
 52|

[P61]

[P62]

[P64]
“…”

[P65]

[P66]

[P67]

[P68]
- The Late Hunter Jung Hyunwoo (pictured)
- Accidents Continue: Gates Remain Deadly Even for A-Rank Hunters
- Myeongdong Guild Expresses Regret over Unexpected Death…

[P69]

[P70]
*The Myeongdong Guild? That’s Jihoon’s Guild.*

[P71]
Just as I was about to take a closer look, Team Leader Choi elegantly tilted his coffee cup and continued.

[P72]
“The Peace Guild will continue to grow. We’ve already recruited twenty B-rank Hunters and thirty C-rank or lower Hunters. That kind of growth is unprecedented in Korea’s long-stagnant market.”

[P73]

[P74]
Only about four months had passed since the Guild was founded, but if we maintained this momentum, we could easily call ourselves a mid-sized Guild.

[P75]
*Of course, we still have far fewer Hunters than other mid-sized Guilds.*

[P76]
That was because we hadn’t recruited more yet, not because we couldn’t.

[P77]

[P78]
“And I played a major role in that. I’m the number one contributor.”

[P79]
“That’s true.”

[P80]
Team Leader Choi continued smoothly.

[P81]
“It is true, but I’m not giving you a bonus.”

[P82]
“…You’re quick to catch on.”

[P83]
I’d tested the waters just in case, but he hadn’t taken the bait.

[P84]
Team Leader Choi smiled as he watched me smack my lips in disappointment.

[P85]
“However, I’ll consider it favorably if you do me one favor.”

[P86]
“What favor?”

[P87]
“I’d like you to take charge of the rookie Guild members for a while.”

[P88]
“…The rookies?”

[P89]
“Yes. We were very selective when we recruited them, and they’re all talented, but they’re still rough around the edges.”

[P90]
“Of course they are. They’re beginners.”

[P91]
No matter how much training someone went through, a real battle felt completely different from the training camp.

[P92]
There was a reason people said a lower-rank Hunter with ten years of experience was better than a higher-rank Hunter fresh out of training camp.

[P93]
“But why ask me? There are other people here.”

[P94]
“I already spoke to Butler Kim and Song-i this morning. I suggested that we take turns teaching the rookies.”

[P95]
“What did they say?”

[P96]
“They agreed. Gladly, without the slightest hesitation.”

[P97]
“…What about Uncle Kkeokjeong?”

[P98]
“I haven’t been able to ask him yet. It’s long past his usual arrival time, and he isn’t answering his phone.”

[P99]
Team Leader Choi checked the time and continued.

[P100]
“Wouldn’t it be a good idea? The rookies are hoping you’ll teach them, too. Most of them applied to our Guild because of you.”

[P101]
“I appreciate the flattery, but…”

[P102]
I scratched the back of my head.

[P103]
Dark Heaven had revealed its fangs in Murim, and Jeok Cheongang was still unconscious.

[P104]
Even if I spent thirty days in the modern world, only three hours would pass in Murim. I had time to spare, but when I could be clearing A-rank Gates, teaching a bunch of greenhorns wasn’t exactly an appealing use of it.

[P105]
If I was going to spend that time on something else, I’d be a hundred times better off with my family.

[P106]
“Leave me out of it. From the Guild’s perspective, wouldn’t it be more efficient for me to clear another A-rank Gate instead of teaching those guys?”

[P107]
“More efficient…”

[P108]
“Yes. Efficiency.”

[P109]
“Then I suppose it can’t be helped.”

[P110]
A sinister smile curled Team Leader Choi’s lips.

[P111]
“I’ll be counting on you to look after our rookies.”

[P112]
“What?”

[P113]
“All the A-rank Gates are booked solid. You won’t get into one for at least a week.”

[P114]
“Don’t lie to me! You scam artist!”

[P115]
“If you don’t believe me, see for yourself.”

[P116]
I snatched the paper Team Leader Choi held out. It was densely packed with the reservation schedules for A-rank Gates across the country.

[P117]
Damn it. He was telling the truth.

[P118]
“I’ll give you a two-hundred-percent performance bonus this month. You get to go on raids and teach your juniors. How wholesome.”

[P119]
“…”

[P120]
“Or you can stay home and do nothing.”

[P121]
The corners of Team Leader Choi’s mouth rose in an infuriating smile.

[P122]
I was just about to shout, *I’m not doing it!*, when a System notification rang.

[P123]
Ding.

[P124]
> **System**
>
> - The Quest **It Was Too Much Money to Say “I’m Not Doing It!”** has been generated!
>
> Will you accept the Quest?
>
> Y   /   N

[P125]
“What do you say?”

[P126]
“…”

[P127]
“I’ll take that as a yes and get the rookies ready. I’ve already reserved several B-rank Gates.”

[P128]
Ding.

[P129]
> **System**
>
> - You have tacitly agreed.
> - You have accepted the Quest!

[P130]
Goddamn it.

[P132]
—Grrrrr.

[P133]
The monsters’ harsh breathing closed in from every direction. Twenty pairs of anxious eyes swept their surroundings.

[P134]
Huff. Huff.

[P135]
Their breathing grew ragged, and their hands turned white around their shields and weapons.

[P136]
Perched on a branch high above the ground, I watched the scene unfold.

[P137]
My face was expressionless, but my mind was occupied by a serious dilemma.

[P138]
*What should I have for dinner?*

[P139]
Galbi, or whole boiled duck for the first time in ages?

[P140]
Both were too good to pass up…

[P141]
“Hold the line!”

[P142]
“Damage dealers, what are you doing?”

[P143]
The shrill screams drew my attention back to the chaos below.

[P144]
More than a dozen Lycanthropes were charging the shield wall and hammering against it. The pale-faced tanks were being driven steadily backward.

[P145]
*Of course they’re getting pushed back. They’re trying to overpower the monsters head-on.*

[P146]
It wasn’t entirely the tanks’ fault, though. The damage dealers were so flustered that they weren’t doing their jobs, either.

[P147]
If they had launched suppressive attacks at the right moments, this situation would never have happened.

[P148]
I’d warned them several times before the raid began, but they were still making the same mistakes.

[P149]
*That line is about to break.*

[P150]
The moment I thought it, the shield wall collapsed amid a chorus of screams.

[P151]
A gap opened in an instant. One particularly agile Lycanthrope charged through with its signature howl.

[P152]
Its bright yellow predator’s eyes fixed on the healers sheltering behind the shield wall.

[P153]
—Graaaargh!

[P154]
—Awoooooo!

[P155]
It sounded like nothing more than dogs barking to me, but the rookies, who were only on their second raid, were terrified.

[P156]
“Aaaah!”

[P157]
“Eeeek!”

[P158]
The mage and healer’s screams shook the dark forest.

[P159]
*It was already noisy enough. Those screams will draw another twenty over here.*

[P160]
I made sure to remember the two screamers.

[P161]
From now on, their nickname would be the Pied Pipers.

[P162]
“Senior! Senior Jin Taekyung!”

[P163]
“Please help us, Senior!”

[P164]
Several round faces looked up at me and cried out desperately.

[P165]
The front line had already collapsed, and the rookies had nothing behind them but an enormous boulder.

[P166]
The Lycanthropes closed in triumphantly, tightening their encirclement.

[P167]
*How are the monsters better at holding formation than they are?*

[P168]
I rubbed the sleep from the corner of my eye and answered.

[P169]
“I told you. If I help, your skills won’t improve.”

[P170]
“We don’t care if they improve!”

[P171]
“Well, I do. You know what happens if you make a habit of getting help? You’ll make a habit of shitting the bed during raids, too.”

[P172]
“We still don’t want to die like this!”

[P173]
“But… nobody wants to die, you know?”

[P174]
“Please help us!”

[P175]
“Don’t give up. Keep fighting. You can do it!”

[P176]
“Please save us!”

[P177]
“By the way, what should I have for dinner—galbi or boiled duck?”

[P178]
“You fucking bastard!”

[P179]
It was the balding rookie from that morning. The admiration that had once shone even brighter than his scalp was gone, replaced by pure fury.

[P180]
“Get down here, you little bastard—”

[P181]
Thud!

[P182]
A tank came flying in from somewhere and crashed into him, sending them both sailing into the distance.

[P183]
Victory had all but gone to the monsters. I was wondering whether it was time to step in when—

[P184]
Shhk!

[P185]
—Kauuugh…

[P186]
A flash of light streaked through the air, and one of the Lycanthropes groaned. Blood gushed from its gaping throat before it crumpled to the ground.

[P187]
The young man who had landed the precise, powerful strike shouted at the top of his lungs.

[P188]
“Formation Three!”

[P189]
His booming voice snapped the others back to their senses one by one.

[P190]
Soon, the twenty Hunters had re-formed their ranks and begun advancing slowly.

[P191]
At their head stood Kim Jinsoo.

[P192]
“Keep pushing! Archers, get your skills ready!”

[P193]
*That kid has potential.*

[P194]
I let out a quiet laugh and jumped down from the tree. Then I swung my spear at the dozens of Lycanthropes drawn by the sound of battle.

[P195]
Whoooosh!

[P196]
* * *

[P197]
“You did well.”

[P198]
“Thank you, Senior!”

[P199]
Kim Jinsoo grinned and bowed. Behind him were three people bent over with their heads down.

[P200]
Two were the Pied Pipers, and the other was the balding rookie.

[P201]
I’d given the balding rookie the special privilege of holding the push-up position.

[P202]
I had to help him protect what little hair he had left…

[P203]
“Keep it up next time. You’ll improve quickly.”

[P204]
“Yes. I won’t disappoint you, Senior.”

[P205]
“Then go get some rest, Jinsoo. We have another raid in two hours.”

[P206]
Team Leader Choi had really gone all out. He’d scheduled three raids in a single day.

[P207]
I was grinding my teeth inwardly when the phone in my pocket began to vibrate.

[P208]
**Designer-Brand Junkie**

[P209]
What was this? Had he read my mind?

[P210]
Still baffled, I answered the call. Team Leader Choi’s urgent voice struck my ear.

[P211]
“Taekyung. Come to the hospital in Ilsan right now!”

[P212]
Hospital?

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.

- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.

Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.
